note: Seeded from main for the owner's 2026-10-02 ruling: "go with cat/cat-harness/todos and cat/cat-harness/beans as their own named sub-graph branches". One special branch per named subgraph of cat-harness, superseding the shared cat/cat-harness/state for this subgraph. REFRESHED 2026-10-04 to the EXACT TREE THE p3ny CUTOVER REMOVES, not to main's tip. That distinction is the whole safety property: beans change on main continuously, because every merged PR carries a claim, a note or a new def, so a seed refreshed from main's tip is stale within minutes and `bun run state:drift` then refuses the cutover - correctly, since a cutover commit replaces the subtree wholesale and would resurrect what the seed held while losing what landed since, with no diff for a reviewer to read. Measured: the prior seed was 24 files behind, and a refresh from the tip was already 3 behind by the time it was verified. So this tree is the cutover branch's own merged beans/ tree, which makes "what is removed" and "what the seed holds" the same object by construction rather than by timing. STILL `seed` AND `authoritative: false` ON PURPOSE: this branch becomes the store at the instant main stops tracking beans/, which is PR #2072; a manifest claiming otherwise while that PR is open would be false for as long as it is open. cat/cat-harness/fsh-guts is the counter-example - its manifest still reads `status: seed` while special-branches.json on main records it authoritative since the 9c7h cutover, so the two disagree and a reader trusting the manifest gets the stale answer. History is not rewritten onto this branch: it stays on main, reachable from source.sha.
